subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway startup fails when SQLite migration target already exists

question: Should verified authoritative-SQLite legacy residue be archived or removed during migration, or intentionally remain on disk with a non-blocking notice?
rationale: Both choices unblock readiness, but they establish different persistent-state, repeat-detection, and operator-visibility contracts across core and bundled plugin migration owners.

options.title: Converge and clean residue
options.body: Archive to a safe non-colliding destination or remove only verified-authoritative legacy sources while preserving warnings for true conflicts.

options.title: Retain with notices
options.body: Leave authoritative legacy sources in place but classify their skip results as notices so gateway readiness is not blocked.

options.title: Pause for canonical policy
options.body: Hold both narrow pull requests until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/103076 settles one convergence rule for every affected source.

recommendation.title: Converge and clean residue
recommendation.body: Archive to a safe non-colliding destination or remove only verified-authoritative legacy sources while preserving warnings for true conflicts.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent predecessor convergence fix makes this person the closest available owner for the cross-migration behavior choice.
